Header: 2027-06-18 16:00 PDT | Duration 52m | Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood CSM), Jordan Miles (AE), Priya Kothari (SE); Dr. Maya Thompson (CTO), Rafael Diaz (Head Eng), Priya Singh (Compliance), Nicole Park (PM)

Summary: Quick onboarding kickoff to align scope, timeline, and owners for Crestfield's Redwood rollout. Discussed deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), compliance requirements (SOC2, data residency), initial POC scope (notes ingestion, conversational triage), and next steps for access and a technical deep dive.

Topics: Onboarding timeline; Access and accounts; Network/VPC and KMS; Initial POC success metrics; Pricing and Dedicated capacity options; Security docs and audit needs.

00:00 Alicia Chen: Okay, hey everyone thanks for hopping on, I'm Alicia from Redwood Customer Success, I'll run through the kickoff agenda, do intros and then hand over to Priya for the tech bits.
00:12 Dr. Maya Thompson: Hi all, Maya here, CTO at Crestfield, excited to get started.
00:18 Rafael Diaz: Rafael--head of eng, we'll own the integration work.
00:22 Nicole Park: Nicole, PM for the triage feature.
00:27 Priya Singh: Priya, compliance. We'll be focused on audit trails and data residency concerns.
00:33 Alicia Chen: Great, Jordan and Priya from Redwood, do quick intros.
00:36 Jordan Miles: Jordan, AE, happy to own procurement and pricing questions.
00:40 Priya Kothari: Priya K from Solutions Engineering, I'll cover architecture and what's needed for a Private/VPC or Dedicated setup.
00:48 Alicia Chen: Agenda—1) confirm goals and timeline, 2) access and accounts, 3) deployment options and constraints, 4) security/compliance checklist, 5) POC scope and success criteria, 6) next steps. Anything to add?
00:58 Dr. Maya Thompson: No, that's it. We have a goal to have a pilot running in four weeks, roughly July 16th. Is that feasible?
01:07 Alicia Chen: Four weeks is ambitious but doable if we get access and network info quickly; we'll plan for a two-week prep and two-week pilot. We'll capture milestones in the playbook.
01:16 Rafael Diaz: Our constraints: on-prem data stores, strict data residency for PHI, and SSO integration. We want the inference to happen on-prem or within our VPC if possible.
01:28 Priya Kothari: Understood. We support three deployment modes—hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra), and Redwood Private (VPC/air-gapped where inference and control plane are in customer network). For PHI, Private or Dedicated are typical. For on-prem we have an on-prem package but we'll need network diagrams and firewall rules.
01:53 Priya Singh: From compliance: SOC 2 reports, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retention, and ability to disable model logging for certain endpoints.
02:03 Alicia Chen: We'll share the security pack and SOC 2, plus our audit log retention options. For KMS we have integrations—bring your own KMS is supported for Private deployments.
02:13 Jordan Miles: On pricing, Dedicated is usually a commit; I'll send tiered options and uplift for VPC/private support.
02:20 Nicole Park: For the pilot our success metric is: 1) ingestion pipeline connects to Redwood and indexes notes into embeddings, 2) triage chat accuracy at > 85% on our eval set, 3) end-to-end latency under 500ms for 95th percentile for triage queries.
02:37 Priya Kothari: Good — we'll validate latency with initial benchmark runs. Important to understand your sequence lengths and concurrency. Rafael, can you share sample traffic patterns?
02:48 Rafael Diaz: Mostly short queries, avg seq length ~120 tokens, peak concurrency ~40 qps in pilot.
02:55 Priya Kothari: That informs batching and instance sizing. We'll propose a config that meets the 95p latency target.
03:03 Alicia Chen: For access: we need a service account with least privilege and an admin contact. We'll send the access checklist. Any SSO provider?
03:12 Dr. Maya Thompson: We use Okta.
03:15 Priya Kothari: Okta's supported; we'll send SAML setup doc. For Private you'll also need to open outbound to our control plane endpoints unless you want fully air-gapped which takes longer.
03:28 Priya Singh: We prefer no data leave the VPC. Is that feasible?
03:33 Priya Kothari: Yes, with Redwood Private you can keep inference inside your VPC and integrate with your KMS and logging—control plane can be customer-hosted. That said, it increases lead time and we'll want to scope it as part of a multi-phase plan (pilot in Dedicated first, then Private).
03:51 Jordan Miles: Many customers do a pilot on Dedicated or hosted with reduced data in requests to validate UX, then move to Private for PHI. That helps speed time-to-value.
04:03 Nicole Park: That sounds reasonable—do we lose any functionality with Dedicated vs Private?
04:09 Priya Kothari: Functionality is largely the same; differences are network controls, KMS ownership, and audit log custody. We also offer model pinning and rollout controls in both.
04:20 Rafael Diaz: On encryption—will we be able to rotate keys and have seamless re-encryption?
04:25 Alicia Chen: Yes, in Private you manage KMS; we support key rotation patterns. We'll include an architecture doc.
04:31 Priya Singh: We need contractual language about data deletion and retention—can you share the standard terms?
04:36 Jordan Miles: I'll attach our data processing addendum and standard retention clauses in the follow-up.
04:42 Alicia Chen: POC scope recap—ingest clinical notes -> embeddings -> triage chat. We'll instrument metrics for latency, cost per token, and quality on your eval set.
04:51 Nicole Park: Do you have an eval harness we can reuse?
04:54 Priya Kothari: Yes, we have a lightweight eval harness and a couple of benchmarking scripts. We'll share a repo link. Expect slight transcription errors in the scripts but functional.
05:05 Dr. Maya Thompson: What about model variants and fallbacks? For critical triage we want graceful degradation if a large model is unavailable.
05:13 Priya Kothari: We support model routing and fallback policies—canary and A/B rollouts plus automatic fallbacks to quantized or smaller variants. We'll include recommended policies for triage.
05:25 Rafael Diaz: Network/NAT and firewall specifics—what ports and IPs?
05:29 Priya Kothari: We'll send a network diagram and a minimal list: outbound TLS to our control plane endpoints (we'll provide IP ranges and DNS), plus setup for private endpoints if using VPC peering. For air-gapped, we'll supply an on-prem deployment manifest.
05:45 Priya Singh: Audit logs—how long are they kept and can we push to our SIEM?
05:50 Alicia Chen: Logs retained per plan—defaults and enterprise retention add-on. We can push logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder for Private deployments. We'll surface options in the security pack.
06:02 Nicole Park: Timeline—if we start this week and provision access quickly, you said ~4 weeks to pilot. What are the first-week deliverables?
06:10 Alicia Chen: Access checklist, onboarding playbook, technical deep dive scheduled, pricing and contract info. We'll aim to get the playbook and checklist today.
06:18 Jordan Miles: I'll follow up on pricing and contract templates within 24 hours.
06:22 Priya Kothari: I'll propose a date for the technical deep dive; we should collect network diagrams and a service account before then.
06:30 Rafael Diaz: We'll try to provision the service account and share diagrams by Monday.
06:35 Alicia Chen: Great. Any blockers from customer side we should know now?
06:39 Priya Singh: Internal legal wants to review SOC2 and DPA before accessing test data.
06:44 Jordan Miles: We'll send SOC2 and DPA; legal review usually takes 3-5 business days. I'll flag the security docs to prioritize.
06:52 Alicia Chen: Ok last part—recap of owners and immediate next steps. Alicia will send playbook and access checklist, Jordan sends pricing and DPA, Priya (SE) schedules technical deep dive and sends network checklist, Rafael will provision service account and share diagrams, Priya (compliance) will review SOC2 when sent.
07:10 Dr. Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone, excited to get started.
07:14 Alicia Chen: Thanks all—I'll send notes and action items right after this call.
07:18 Meeting ended.

References shared: onboarding_playbook.pdf (link sent), security_pack_SOC2_v2.pdf (link), network_checklist.xlsx (link), eval_harness_repo (link).
